text:
nina-cs: Heads up — Acme reported rerank outputs that look like raw logits (negatives and >1). Customer expected probabilities in [0,1]. They also hit a separate 400 when sending 120 candidates.

priya-ml: can you paste the exact request+response (redact api key) and which model/endpoint? also did they use batch or single request?

nina-cs: pasted below (redacted):
```
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "query": "best onboarding flow",
  "candidates": [ ... 78 items ... ]
}

Response 200:
{
  "scores": [-10.45, -0.2, 0.7, 3.14, -2.1],
  "candidate_ids": [..]
}
```
They said client code treats higher score as better and expected values between 0 and 1.

sam-eng: quick answers:
- The rerank endpoint returns model "scores" as raw ranking logits by default (architecture-dependent). These are not probabilities and can be negative or >1. Higher = better, but values are arbitrary units.
- We don't normalize automatically because different downstream use-cases want raw scores for re-scaling or custom combos.

felix-support: customer asked whether billing depends on score magnitude — no, billing is per-call/token not affected by numeric score values.

priya-ml: steps to repro for us:
1) paste the exact JSON body used
2) include model name (e.g., rust-rr-1b) and api_version if present
3) confirm candidate count (we have a hard per-request candidate cap at 64 currently)

nina-cs: they actually sent 78 candidates which explains the 400. I told them to page to <=64 and retry.

sam-eng: guidance to share with customer:
- Interpretation: treat scores as relative. If you need probabilities, apply softmax across the candidate set. Example: 
```python
scores = [-10.45, -0.2, 0.7, 3.14, -2.1]
import math
exp = [math.exp(s) for s in scores]
probs = [e / sum(exp) for e in exp]
# probs now in [0,1] and sum to 1
```
- If you want per-candidate independent confidence in [0,1] (not mutually exclusive), use a calibration / sigmoid on each score or run a separate binary eval model.
- Endpoint option: add "normalize": "softmax" in request to get normalized probs server-side (available on rerank v2 for select models).

priya-ml: also note numeric stability: for very negative logits you should do max-subtraction before exp to avoid underflow: 
```python
mx = max(scores)
exp = [math.exp(s - mx) for s in scores]
probs = [e / sum(exp) for e in exp]
```

sam-eng: TL;DR to send customer:
1) Scores are raw logits (higher better), can be negative, not bounded.
2) To get 0-1 probabilities use softmax (we show code) or use "normalize":"softmax" on supported models.
3) Candidate limit is 64 — page candidates or pre-filter to avoid 400.
4) Billing unaffected by score magnitudes.

felix-support: customer replied: "ok makes sense, please enable server-side normalize for our account if possible" — I asked for account id and model; flagged to enterprise-ops if they want account-level toggle. :+1:

rerank-bot: NOTE: recorded incident stub #CS-8971 for follow-up (docs link: https://redwood.ai/docs/rerank#scores).

nina-cs: leaving action items:
- felix to collect account id + model for enablement (felix)
- priya to add a small example to docs showing softmax + numeric-stability note (priya)
- sam to confirm candidate-limit wording in API error text is clear and suggests paging (sam)

priya-ml: I'll PR the docs example today.

sam-eng: I'll tweak the 400 message to say: "too many candidates (max 64). paginate or pre-filter and retry"

nina-cs: thanks all — marking this resolved from CS side unless we hear otherwise from the customer. :white_check_mark:
